## Fix claim tree cleanup when deleting nodes and edges

When a user deletes a node from the graph, any edges connected to that node are also deleted. However, the claim trees (nodes and edges that argue for a deleted part, identified by `arguedDiagramPartId`) for those related, deleted parts are not being cleaned up properly. Currently, the code only deletes the claim tree for the single part being deleted, but not for any other parts that are also being removed as a consequence (e.g., edges connected to the deleted node).

    The goal is to ensure that when a node or edge is deleted, all claim trees for all parts that are being removed (directly or as a consequence) are also deleted. The simplest approach is to delete the primary graph part(s), then run a general cleanup that removes any claim nodes/edges whose `arguedDiagramPartId` no longer exists in the graph.

    Please modify the delete logic in `src/web/topic/store/createDeleteActions.ts`:
    1. In `deleteNode`: remove the node and its connected edges (without filtering by `arguedDiagramPartId`), then call a new `deleteInvalidClaims` helper.
    2. In `deleteEdge`: remove just the edge (without filtering by `arguedDiagramPartId`), then call the same `deleteInvalidClaims` helper.
    3. Implement `deleteInvalidClaims`, which builds a list of all remaining node/edge IDs and filters out any claim nodes/edges whose `arguedDiagramPartId` is not in that list.
    4. Note the special case in `deleteNode` for `rootClaim` nodes: this already correctly deletes the entire claim tree for the argued part, so no changes are needed there.

    This change should be contained to `src/web/topic/store/createDeleteActions.ts` — no other files need to be modified.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` for the dependencies and available scripts (e.g., test, lint, typecheck). The project uses a `vitest.config.ts` for test configuration, and there are existing test files under `src/api/routers/` (e.g., `topic.test.ts`). Refer to `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general contribution guidelines, and `package.json` scripts for how to run tests and checks.

## Implementation Plan
1. Open `src/web/topic/store/createDeleteActions.ts`.
    2. In the `deleteNode` function (in the non-rootClaim branch):
       - Change the `state.nodes` filter to only remove the node by ID: `state.nodes = state.nodes.filter((node) => node.id !== nodeId)`.
       - Change the `state.edges` filter to only remove edges connected to the node: `state.edges = state.edges.filter((edge) => !nodeEdges.includes(edge))`.
       - After those filters, call `deleteInvalidClaims(state)` before `deleteInvalidScores(state)`.
    3. In the `deleteEdge` function:
       - Change the `state.nodes` filter to no longer run — instead only filter edges: `state.edges = state.edges.filter((edge) => edge.id !== edgeId)`.
       - Call `deleteInvalidClaims(state)` before `deleteInvalidScores(state)`.
    4. Add a new helper function `deleteInvalidClaims(state: TopicStoreState)` near `deleteInvalidScores`:
       - Build an array of all remaining graph part IDs: `const graphPartIds = [...state.nodes, ...state.edges].map((graphPart) => graphPart.id)`.
       - Filter `state.nodes` to keep only nodes where `node.data.arguedDiagramPartId === undefined` OR that ID is in `graphPartIds`.
       - Filter `state.edges` to keep only edges where `edge.data.arguedDiagramPartId === undefined` OR that ID is in `graphPartIds`.
       - Use `/* eslint-disable functional/immutable-data, no-param-reassign */` comments as in the surrounding code.
    5. Ensure the existing `deleteInvalidScores` helper remains unchanged.

197:     return (

199:       (edge.source === child.id && edge.target === parent.id)

201:   });

205:     return false;
206:   }
207: 
208:   if (existingEdge) {

210:     return false;
211:   }
212: 
213:   const secondParentForClaim =
214:     claimNodeTypes.includes(child.type) &&
215:     topicGraph.edges.find((edge) => edge.target === child.id);
216:   if (secondParentForClaim) {
217:     console.log("cannot connect nodes: claims are in a tree so can't have multiple parents");
218:     return false;
219:   }
220: 
221:   if (!relation) {
222:     console.log("cannot connect nodes: nodes don't form a valid relation");
223:     return false;

251: // see algorithm pseudocode & example at https://github.com/amelioro/ameliorate/issues/66#issuecomment-1465078133
252: export const isEdgeAShortcut = (edge: Edge, topicGraph: Graph) => {
253:   const edgeParent = parentNode(edge, topicGraph.nodes);
254:   const edgeChild = childNode(edge, topicGraph.nodes);
255: 
256:   return shortcutRelations.some((shortcutRelation) => {
257:     const edgeCouldBeAShortcut =
258:       edgeParent.type === shortcutRelation.relation.parent &&
259:       edgeChild.type === shortcutRelation.relation.child;
260: 
261:     if (!edgeCouldBeAShortcut) return false;
262: 
263:     const childrenOfParent = children(edgeParent, topicGraph);
264:     const parentsOfChild = parents(edgeChild, topicGraph);
265: 
266:     const detourNodeAsChild = childrenOfParent.find(
267:       (child) => child.type === shortcutRelation.detourNodeType
268:     );
269:     const detourNodeAsParent = parentsOfChild.find(
270:       (parent) => parent.type === shortcutRelation.detourNodeType
271:     );
272: 
273:     // note: does not check if detour node is showing - this is so that hidden shortcut edges
274:     // can still be shown when a detour node is hidden
275:     const detourNodeConnectsParentAndChild = detourNodeAsChild && detourNodeAsParent;
276: 
277:     return detourNodeConnectsParentAndChild;
278:   });
279: };

283:  * can still be shown when a component node is hidden
284:  */

286:   const edgeParent = parentNode(edge, topicGraph.nodes);
287:   const edgeChild = childNode(edge, topicGraph.nodes);
288: 
289:   // check implied through parent
290:   const componentsOfParent = components(edgeParent, topicGraph);
291:   const impliedThroughParentComponent = componentsOfParent.some((component) => {
292:     return topicGraph.edges.some(
293:       (edge) =>
294:         edge.source === component.id && edge.label === edge.label && edge.target === edgeChild.id
295:     );
296:   });
297: 
298:   if (impliedThroughParentComponent) return true;
299: 
300:   // check implied through child
301:   const componentsOfChild = components(edgeChild, topicGraph);
302:   const impliedThroughChildComponent = componentsOfChild.some((component) => {
303:     return topicGraph.edges.some(
304:       (edge) =>
305:         edge.target === component.id && edge.label === edge.label && edge.source === edgeParent.id
306:     );
307:   });
308: 
309:   return impliedThroughChildComponent;
310: };

315: // edges should not be implied based on the user viewing them.
316: //
317: // We don't want users to apply scores and then never see them again due to an implied edge being
318: // hidden. The button to show implied edges should reduce this pain, but maybe we need a better view
319: // to reduce the need to hide implied edges?

321:   if (claimRelationNames.includes(edge.label)) return false; // claims can't be implied
322:   if (hasClaims(edge, claimEdges)) return false;
323: 
324:   return isEdgeAShortcut(edge, displayDiagram) || isEdgeImpliedByComposition(edge, displayDiagram);

1: # State Management Patterns
2: 
3: Zustand stores are used to manage front-end state. Check out the [Zustand documentation](https://docs.pmnd.rs/zustand/getting-started/introduction) for details about how it works. There are a few different pieces that make up our state management: the store, its actions, and its hooks.
4: 
5: ## The store itself
6: 
7: This has the state in it
8: 
9: ## Actions
10: 
11: These are functions that update the state
12: 
13: - generally these should be invoked from a component (e.g. clicking the add node button will invoke the addNode action)
14: - some actions just read the current state (different from hooks because they don't subscribe to changes)
15: - these follow the [separate actions from store pattern](https://docs.pmnd.rs/zustand/guides/practice-with-no-store-actions)
16: - generally these will look something like
17: 
18:   ```ts
19:   const action = () => {
20:     // Using immer's `createDraft` allows us to mutate a draft object instead of the store's current
21:     // state object.
22:     const state = createDraft(useTopicStore.getState());
23: 
24:     // Do something with the state (usually mutating it because the very-nested state is annoying to update without mutation).
25:     // We use this pattern instead of the suggested `setState((state) => [modifiedState])` so that
26:     // we can use async functions, like `layout`.
27: 
28:     // `finishDraft` returns a new object with all the modifications, and maintains nested object
29:     // object references for objects that were not modified. This reduces re-renders for hooks that
30:     // rely on `Object.is` for comparison.
31:     useTopicStore.setState(finishDraft(state), false, "[actionName]");
32:   };
33:   ```
34: 
35: ## Hooks
36: 
37: These are functions that subscribe to changes in the state
38: 
39: - generally these should be used from a component to render something based on state in the store - when the hook returns a different value, the component will re-render
40: - these follow the [only export custom hooks pattern](https://tkdodo.eu/blog/working-with-zustand#only-export-custom-hooks), so components shouldn't need to select state (`useStore((state) => state.diagrams)`) from the store directly
41: - these will look something like
42: 
43:   ```ts
44:   const useDiagram = (diagramId: string) => {
45:     return useTopicStore((state) => state.diagrams[diagramId]);
46:   };
47:   ```
48: 
49: - note: for hooks that copy an object or create a new array, and therefore have new object/array
50:   references, consider passing a shallow comparison fn to prevent extra re-renders (see zustand [docs](https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand#selecting-multiple-state-slices))
51: 
52: ### Zombie child issue
53: 
54: - hooks should generally not throw errors, particularly due to the [zombie child issue](https://github.com/pmndrs/zustand/issues/302)
55:   - e.g. if a node is deleted from state, the node's component will have a re-render triggered due to the state change, but hooks looking for that node will not find it; in this case, the hook should just return something that doesn't error - the node's component will soon be removed from the DOM by re-render of the parent Diagram component

## What changed

**`src/web/view/navigateStore.ts`** (new URL-sync section, lines 156–287)
- `navigationStateToSearchParams` / `searchParamsToNavigationState` — pure serialization between the navigate store state and query params:
  - `selectedGraphPart` → `selectedGraphPartId`
  - `viewExploreDiagram=true` → `viewingExploreDiagram`
  - `tableProblem=<id>` → `viewingCriteriaTable` + `activeTableProblemId` (flag implied by param presence, since the store always sets an id when the flag is true)
  - `claimTreeId=<id>` → `viewingClaimTree` + `activeClaimTreeId`
- `useSyncUrlViewState` (called from `TopicWorkspace.tsx:22`), which:
  - **reads** params on mount (the workspace only mounts after `populateFromApi`/`populateFromLocalStorage` runs `resetNavigationState`, so restore happens after the reset — the handoff's ordering concern is handled)
  - **validates** restored ids against the loaded topic store (`useTopicStore.getState()`), dropping stale `tableProblem`/`claimTreeId`/`selectedGraphPart` values and their flags — preventing the empty-overlay/click-swallowing bug PR 309 fixed
  - **updates the URL** via `history.pushState` on every navigate-store change, but only when the serialized state differs from the current URL, so URL-originated updates don't create new entries
  - **restores on `popstate`**, so browser back/forward drives view navigation
  - clears the navigate store's zundo history after URL restores, consistent with "page loads aren't undoable"

## Key design points
- URL is a mirror; the navigate store remains the source of truth, and the existing `resetNavigationState()` flow is untouched.
- Stale-state correctness: closing a table/claim tree leaves the id set but the flag false, so serialization gates id params on flags, and restore sets flags strictly from the params.
- Page transitions aren't broken: the workspace unmounts whenever topic data switches to loading (Next route change), so no stale subscription pushes or restores during cross-topic navigation.

- No `node_modules`/network/db, so verification is by inspection plus `tsc --ignoreConfig` syntax pass — the only reported errors are missing-module cascades (TS2307) and their implicit-`any` fallout on pre-existing lines.

Implement two new node types, "benefit" and "detriment", for use in the topic diagram. These represent positive and negative outcomes of solutions respectively, complementing the existing "effect" node type. The new types should be fully integrated throughout the stack: database schema, API types, diagram rendering, theming, node behavior (relations, addability), and layout partitioning.

    Key behavior requirements:
    - Benefits and detriments should behave like effects in terms of being creatable from problems and having solutions create them.
    - They should have appropriate visual distinction: benefits with a green-ish tint (analogous to effect/solution/support) and detriments with a pink/magenta tint (analogous to effect/problem/critique).
    - Layout partitioning must be dynamic: a benefit/detriment connected to a problem on one side and a solution on the other should be placed between them (unpartitioned); if only connected to a problem, it should be in an early partition (0); otherwise, later (2).

11:   problem: "null",
12:   criterion: "1",
13:   effect: "2",

25:   support: "null",
26:   critique: "null",
27: 
28:   // generic
29:   custom: "null",
30: };
31: 
32: const priorities = Object.fromEntries(nodeTypes.map((type, index) => [type, index.toString()])) as {
33:   [type in NodeType]: string;
34: };
35: 
36: const elk = new ELK();
37: 
38: // sort by source priority, then target priority
39: const compareEdges = (edge1: Edge, edge2: Edge, nodes: Node[]) => {
40:   const source1 = nodes.find((node) => node.id === edge1.source);
41:   const source2 = nodes.find((node) => node.id === edge2.source);
42:   const target1 = nodes.find((node) => node.id === edge1.target);
43:   const target2 = nodes.find((node) => node.id === edge2.target);
44: 
45:   if (!source1 || !source2 || !target1 || !target2)
46:     throw new Error("Edge source or target not found");
47: 
48:   const sourceCompare = Number(priorities[source1.type]) - Number(priorities[source2.type]);
49:   if (sourceCompare !== 0) return sourceCompare;
50: 
51:   return Number(priorities[target1.type]) - Number(priorities[target2.type]);
52: };
53: 
54: export interface NodePosition {
55:   id: string;
56:   x: number;
57:   y: number;
58: }
59: 
60: export const layout = async (
61:   nodes: Node[],
62:   edges: Edge[],
63:   orientation: Orientation
64: ): Promise<NodePosition[]> => {
65:   // see support layout options at https://www.eclipse.org/elk/reference/algorithms/org-eclipse-elk-layered.html
66:   const layoutOptions: LayoutOptions = {
67:     algorithm: "layered",
68:     "elk.direction": orientation,
69:     // results in a more centered layout - seems to moreso ignore edges when laying out
70:     "elk.edgeRouting": "POLYLINE",
71:     "elk.spacing.edgeEdge": "0",
72:     // other placement strategies seem to either spread nodes out too much, or ignore edges between layers
73:     "elk.layered.nodePlacement.strategy": "NETWORK_SIMPLEX",
74:     // allows grouping nodes by type (within a layer) when edges are sorted by type
75:     // tried using `position` to do this but it doesn't group nodes near their source node
76:     "elk.layered.considerModelOrder.strategy": "NODES_AND_EDGES",
77:     // these spacings are just what roughly seem to look good
78:     "elk.layered.spacing.nodeNodeBetweenLayers": orientation === "DOWN" ? "130" : "220",
79:     "elk.spacing.nodeNode": orientation === "DOWN" ? "20" : "50",
80:     // allow nodes to be partitioned into layers by type
81:     "elk.partitioning.activate": "true",
82:     // ensure node islands don't overlap (needed for when node has 3 rows of text)
83:     "elk.spacing.componentComponent": "30", // default is 20
84:   };
85: 
86:   const graph: ElkNode = {
87:     id: "elkgraph",
88:     children: nodes.map((node) => {
89:       return {
90:         id: node.id,
91:         width: nodeWidthPx,
92:         height: nodeHeightPx,
93:         layoutOptions: {
94:           // Allow nodes to be partitioned into layers by type.
95:           // This can get awkward if there are multiple problems with their own sets of criteria,
96:           // solutions, components, effects; we might be able to improve that situation by modeling
97:           // each problem within a nested node. Or maybe we could just do partitioning within
98:           // a special "problem context view" rather than in the main topic diagram view.
99:           "elk.partitioning.partition": partitionOrders[node.type],
100:         },
101:       };
102:     }),
103:     edges: [...edges]
104:       // This order results in grouping nodes by type under their source node.
105:       // This is a requirement for the claim tree but less so for the topic diagram - if performance
106:       // in the diagram is a concern, this can probably just be done in the tree (and maybe `position`
107:       // would be more suited for the diagram, see https://github.com/kieler/elkjs/issues/21#issuecomment-382574679).
108:       .sort((edge1, edge2) => compareEdges(edge1, edge2, nodes))
109:       .map((edge) => {
110:         return { id: edge.id, sources: [edge.source], targets: [edge.target] };
111:       }),
112:   };
113: 
114:   // hack to try laying out without partition if partitions cause error
115:   // see https://github.com/eclipse/elk/issues/969
116:   try {
117:     const layoutedGraph = await elk.layout(graph, {
118:       layoutOptions,
119:       logging: true,
120:       measureExecutionTime: true,
121:     });
122: 
123:     // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion
124:     return layoutedGraph.children!.map((node) => {
125:       // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion
126:       return { id: node.id, x: node.x!, y: node.y! };
127:     });
128:   } catch (error) {
129:     const layoutedGraph = await elk.layout(graph, {
130:       layoutOptions: { ...layoutOptions, "elk.partitioning.activate": "false" },
131:       logging: true,
132:       measureExecutionTime: true,
133:     });
134: 
135:     // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-non-null-assertion

139:     });

    Currently, the criteria table displays individual scores for each criterion-solution pair, but there is no summary view of how each solution performs overall. Users need a quick, digestible number that indicates whether a solution is good or bad overall, weighted by criterion importance.
